question: Should OpenClaw adopt four built-in hosting profiles and the accompanying public plugin readiness-criterion API as a supported core contract after the readiness prerequisites land?
rationale: This is a new configuration, CLI, environment, protocol, release-automation, and plugin SDK surface; code review cannot determine whether those permanent product contracts belong in core or what compatibility promise maintainers intend.

options.title: Sponsor the staged core contract
options.body: Approve the readiness API direction, land the prerequisite contracts in order, and require exact-head package-installed Docker proof before accepting the profile layer.

options.title: Narrow the scope
options.body: Keep the readiness framework private or operator-configured and remove the new public plugin API and built-in profile contract from this branch.

options.title: Pause the proposal
options.body: Defer hosting profiles until an RFC or maintainer decision establishes the supported deployment-contract boundary.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the staged core contract
recommendation.body: Approve the readiness API direction, land the prerequisite contracts in order, and require exact-head package-installed Docker proof before accepting the profile layer.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the only evidence-backed contributor who has carried the linked readiness and hosting-profile proposal stack; maintainer sponsorship remains necessary.
